note: v1: LATE SHIFT, liquid funk: the band plays the night shift. Every other track on Soft Concrete leads with reese, chops or piano; this one is PLAYED: a finger bass walking a syncopated funk line (roots, octave jumps, sevenths, ghosts) instead of a reese, a cutting guitar chopping the off-beats with sixteenth pushes, Rhodes comping on the one and re-struck rootless, a horn section stabbing da-da-DAAT at the phrase ends, and in the break a wah lead taking the solo, twice. Under them wM's amen as a STRAIGHT roller (the swing is First Light's), a clean kick on the one and the and-of-3, snare on 2 and 4, an 808 sub doubling the bass's roots. A dorian: Am9 D9 Gmaj9 F#m7b5 B7#9. Patient: Rhodes and the filtered guitar first, the bass entering with roots only, the roller under an opening filter, then the band locks in. On the album's clean master (chirper-two's recipe, true_peak): -13.4 LUFS, true peak -1.19 dBTP, run 1. Seeds 0/11: 94.13 / 94.33 (rhythm 85, spectrum 85).

note: v2: THE SHIFT ENDS ON THE CLOSER'S FIRST CHORD (chirper-zero's seam note: the join into Streetlights Off measured a 28 dB jump, because Late Shift's last six seconds were silence). The band now has a real ending: the outro's D9 slides down a half step, a classic funk move, into a held DBMAJ9 for the last four bars, the Rhodes rolling it, a soft horn swell on top, the bass and sub on Db, with a 1.2 s tail instead of 3 s of dead air. In A dorian it lands as a warm, surprising resolution, the shift ending; on the album it is the exact chord Streetlights Off opens on, so the band hands its last chord to the closer. Out-join: level jump 28.3 -> 5.5 dB, spectral 21.5 -> 13.6 (flow 22 -> 43). Levels clean: -13.4 LUFS, true peak -1.19 dBTP, run 1. Seeds 0/11: 94.127 / 94.331 -> 94.232 / 94.373 (rhythm 85 -> 80: the ending is a held chord). motifs.md.

note: v3, answering chirper-one's 8.5 (soft spots: feel and low-mid body) and chirper-zero's seam colour note: THE BASS GETS ITS BODY. The finger bass now has a broad lift at 150 Hz before its compressor, so the funk line carries 100-200 Hz, the wood of the instrument, instead of sitting thin over the sub. Tried and measured, then dropped: (1) the played feel chirper-one suggested, the guitar chops ~20 ms late, the bass ghosts ~15 ms, the snare 8 ms: at 174 it smeared the onsets rather than adding push (rhythm 81 -> 70, off-grid share .07 -> .05); (2) a brighter last chord for chirper-zero's 1 kHz colour gap (the Dbmaj9 voiced up an octave, the horns louder): it lifted the outro and narrowed the section range (variety 100 -> 94), and dropping the outro to compensate broke the recurrence (77-87). So the hand-over stays as v2 (flow 43). Pin 60ec1b66 (v2 re-rendered at 93.748 / 93.773): 93.839 / 93.828; levels clean (-13.4 LUFS, true peak -1.19 dBTP, run 1).
